concepts.def: Behaviour breaking the formal laws of a society and punishable by the state; varies across time and place.
Behaviour breaking informal norms but not always laws; relative to time, place and audience.
Durkheim (1895): crime is inevitable and functional; boundary maintenance, social change, adaptation.
Merton (1938): blocked legitimate routes to success cause innovation (crime); also retreatism, ritualism, rebellion, conformity.
Becker (1963) Outsiders: deviance results from successful application of a label rather than the act itself.
Crime is a product of capitalist inequality; selective enforcement targets working-class crimes over corporate harm.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Sociology of Crime & Deviance — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Sociology of Crime & Deviance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Sociology of Crime & Deviance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Merton
Becker
Cohen

mcqs.q: Labelling theory was developed by Becker in:

options: A reconstituted family is a family living in temporary housing.
A family formed when partners with children from previous relationships come together — a 'blended' or step-family — one of several family forms recognised in family diversity literature.
Organised crime by criminal masterminds.
A reconstituted family is one that has been put back together after divorce.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between reliability and validity in research?
options: Reliable and valid mean the same thing — that the research is good.
Organised crime by criminal masterminds.
Reliability is whether a method produces consistent results when repeated; validity is whether it actually measures what it claims to. A method can be reliable but invalid, or valid but unreliable.
Reliable research is published in journals; valid research isn't.

mcqs.q: What is the 'dark figure' of crime?
options: Reliable research is published in journals; valid research isn't.
Organised crime by criminal masterminds.
Crimes committed at night.
The amount of crime that is unreported or unrecorded.
